item.title: Taiwan accuses China of pressuring Papua New Guinea to expel Taiwanese diplomats

item.content:encoded:
Taiwan accuses China of pressuring Papua New Guinea to expel Taiwanese diplomats During a legislative hearing on Thursday, Lin Hung-hsun, Deputy Director-General of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Department of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, said PNG initially demanded the closure of Taiwan's representative office on July 16, citing its adherence to the "one-China" policy. ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 21:53 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 21:53 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan has accused China of pressuring Papua New Guinea (PNG) to expel Taiwanese diplomats and shut down its representative office in Port Moresby, alleging that Beijing may have used economic incentives to influence the Pacific nation's sudden diplomatic decision, according to a report by Central News Agency (CNA). During a legislative hearing on Thursday, Lin Hung-hsun, Deputy Director-General of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Department of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, said PNG initially demanded the closure of Taiwan's representative office on July 16, citing its adherence to the "one-China" policy. According to CNA, Taiwan and PNG subsequently held discussions and reached an understanding that PNG would provide one year's written notice before the representative office was closed. However, on November 6, PNG reportedly reversed its earlier position and demanded that Taiwanese diplomats leave the country within seven days. Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi told lawmakers that Taiwan believed the sudden change in PNG's position was driven by pressure from Beijing. He pointed to a recent visit by a high-level PNG delegation to China and the upcoming visit of PNG Prime Minister James Marape to China to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. "Given these circumstances, our assessment is that the government of Papua New Guinea may have been subjected to significant pressure from China or even offered economic incentives," Chen said, as cited by CNA. Chen also highlighted China's announcement that it was prepared to increase imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from PNG. This came after Taiwan decided to stop purchasing LNG from the Pacific nation following its demand to close the Taiwanese representative office. The diplomatic dispute concerns the Taiwan Economic Office, which was established in Port Moresby in 1990. On November 6, PNG's Department of Foreign Affairs announced that its secretary, Elias Wohengu, had instructed the office's head, Chiu Chen-yu, and First Secretary Lee Chung-nun to leave the country within seven days. The remaining diplomat, Pan Shao-jyun, was permitted to stay to oversee the office's closure within a year. PNG's foreign affairs department also clarified that although Taiwan had been given 12 months to complete the closure, this should not be interpreted as a guarantee that existing staffing and operational arrangements would remain unchanged during that period. In response, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) announced that it would shut down the representative office and withdraw all personnel stationed in PNG. The ministry also said it would conduct a comprehensive review and adjustment of its relations with PNG, taking into account Taiwan's national dignity, diplomatic autonomy and overall national interests. According to CNA, Taiwan has since begun withdrawing its diplomatic and technical mission personnel from the Pacific nation. PNG maintains diplomatic relations with China, which follows a policy of not allowing its diplomatic allies to maintain simultaneous official diplomatic relations with Taiwan. The latest developments have further highlighted Beijing's diplomatic pressure on countries maintaining or considering engagement with Taipei. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Mossad official arrives in US for high-level talks as Netanyahu pushes for resumed war against Iran: Report However, Trump has so far resisted this pressure, choosing instead to align with Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, and other Gulf nations to maintain a naval blockade and economic pressure campaign while exploring the possibility of a deal. ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 20:51 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 20:51 IST

US President Donald Trump with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

As Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushes the Trump administration to resume military action against Iran, one of his closest confidants and a top Israeli spy agency Mossad official is holding high-stakes talks in Washington and Miami with senior US officials. According to Axios, Roman Gofman, a top confidant of Netanyahu and a director within Mossad, is visiting Washington on Friday to meet with senior US President Donald Trump administration officials, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe and White House envoy Steve Witkoff, regarding the war in Iran. As detailed by Axios, Prime Minister Netanyahu has been pressing President Trump to resume military action against Iran. However, Trump has so far resisted this pressure, choosing instead to align with Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, and other Gulf nations to maintain a naval blockade and economic pressure campaign while exploring the possibility of a deal. Quoted by Axios, President Trump stated on Thursday, "I could end it immediately. At the request of the nations that I'm looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a little bit more civilly." Trump added, "Saudi Arabia has asked me to please just let it be the way it is now for a while, because [Iran is] disintegrating. Qatar, Kuwait, UAE, Bahrain, all of them would much prefer the waiting period." On the other hand, Iran warned countries against providing military or logistical assistance to the United States for its operations against Tehran, saying any such support would be considered a hostile act and make the countries concerned responsible for aggression against the Islamic Republic. Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei issued the warning in a post on X, invoking international law and the United Nations Charter to caution governments against becoming involved in the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. “A sparrow that tries to fly after a stork will eventually break its legs (Korean proverb),” Baghaei said, warning countries against supporting Washington's military actions. He said, “Any direct or indirect involvement in acts of aggression or in inhumane economic terrorism against Iran - including the deployment of naval forces, military and logistical support equipment, and personnel - will be regarded as a hostile and unlawful act amounting to participation in the US aggression against Iran. Such actions not only violate Article 2 (4) of the Charter of the United Nations but also fall within the definition of an act of aggression set out in UN General Assembly Resolution 3314.” Rejecting possible justifications for such assistance, Baghaei said, “Invoking seemingly legitimate pretexts such as “protecting freedom of navigation” or “countering piracy” does not alter the unlawful and hostile nature of such actions.” “Our message is unequivocal: No bilateral agreement or commitment with the United States can constitute legitimate grounds for violating a state’s obligations under international law or for participating in the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran,” he said. Baghaei further added, “Any state that may participate in such unlawful aggressions, in whatever form, shall bear full responsibility for the resulting repercussions.” The developments come at a time of political uncertainty for Netanyahu, following the October 27 general election, which failed to deliver a clear majority to the incumbent Prime Minister's camp. Gadi Eisenkot emerged with the highest number of seats, although no political party secured an outright majority. Israeli President Isaac Herzog subsequently invited Eisenkot on Sunday to form the next government. Eisenkot has been given 28 days to explore possible political arrangements and attempt to put together a minority government, adding another layer of uncertainty to Israel's political landscape. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
"Legal matter, will be dealt with accordingly: MEA on Sheikh Hasina's extradition Addressing the broader trajectory of India-Bangladesh relations, particularly after the fifth round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue scheduled in Dhaka for November 17–18 was postponed, Jaiswal emphasised that New Delhi continues to engage with Dhaka across multiple institutional frameworks. ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 20:26 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 20:26 IST

Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India on Friday maintained that the extradition of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is a "legal matter" that will be handled accordingly, even as it reiterated its desire for a "positive, constructive and forward-looking" relationship with Dhaka following the postponement of bilateral consular talks. Responding to media queries during a weekly briefing amid demands from Dhaka for the ousted leader's return, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal kept New Delhi's position brief and anchored in due process. "Extradition is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly," Jaiswal said. Addressing the broader trajectory of India-Bangladesh relations, particularly after the fifth round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue scheduled in Dhaka for November 17–18 was postponed, Jaiswal emphasised that New Delhi continues to engage with Dhaka across multiple institutional frameworks. "India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh. Accordingly, initiatives have been taken and meetings held under structured mechanisms in areas such as trade, railways, water resources and border management, among others," he stated. Confirming that the postponed consular talks will be rescheduled, the spokesperson noted that revised travel arrangements will be on the agenda once both sides finalise a date. "The next round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, which will also take up matters relating to revised travel arrangements, will be held on a mutually convenient date. India remains ready to discuss all matters and bilateral issues with Bangladesh through these existing mechanisms, including at the technical level. The Consular Dialogue will be held on a mutually convenient date," Jaiswal added. This comes as Hasina, who is residing in India, has asked for her passport and national ID card back from the Bangladesh Embassy in New Delhi to facilitate her planned return to the country in December, which the ruling BNP has described as a political stunt, saying that this kind of move misleads the public and aims to create instability in the country. They believe Sheikh Hasina won’t succeed in this attempt, noting that the people of Bangladesh ousted her through a mass uprising, that her time in politics is over, and that legal action will be taken against her. "Sheikh Hasina is making these moves, such as asking for her passport, to create instability. These actions have been rejected by the people of Bangladesh; she carried out mass killings in Bangladesh and took refuge in India. There is already a national consensus in Bangladesh that Sheikh Hasina’s political role here has been rejected. She is accused of crimes against humanity, as well as abductions, murders, and other serious offences. Therefore, she has no chance of entering politics in Bangladesh anymore", Khsirul Kabir Khokon MP, Joint Secretary General of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), told ANI over the phone. "Unable to tolerate these positive changes, she is making political stunts and making baseless statements. She has no future in Bangladeshi politics—people have already rejected her. Politically, she is a dead horse," Khokon said. This marks her first such communication since fleeing to India in August 2024 following a deadly uprising that ended her 15-year rule. (ANI)

item.title: "F the Iranian leadership. I'm not gonna be cowered": Scott Bessent confirms relocation to military base amid Iranian threats
item.description: While confirming his move to a military installation, Bessent also accused The Wall Street Journal of endangering his safety by publishing a photograph of his Georgetown property shortly after he ...
item.content:encoded:
"F the Iranian leadership. I'm not gonna be cowered": Scott Bessent confirms relocation to military base amid Iranian threats While confirming his move to a military installation, Bessent also accused The Wall Street Journal of endangering his safety by publishing a photograph of his Georgetown property shortly after he purchased it, despite appeals from his team not to disclose its location. ANI | Updated: 13-11-2026 19:56 IST | Created: 13-11-2026 19:56 IST

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has confirmed that he relocated from his Washington residence to a military base on Secret Service instructions following Iranian death threats, delivering a blunt rebuke to Tehran's leadership and criticising The Wall Street Journal for publishing a geolocatable image of his home. Speaking during an interview on CNBC, Bessent said the threats against him and fellow cabinet members show that Washington's economic pressure campaign against Tehran, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast", is taking a toll. "You know what I gotta say, is F the Iranian leadership. I'm not gonna be cowered that they have initiated death threats against me, other members of the cabinet. We're not gonna be cowered, and it means what we are doing with Operation Economic Outcast is working," Bessent told CNBC. Drawing comparisons to the risks faced by American troops stationed in the Persian Gulf and President Donald Trump, Bessent described Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as increasingly desperate under mounting financial isolation. "And, you know, why am I gonna be afraid when our brave military personnel in the Gulf, President Trump constantly receives death threats? And, you know, what we are doing is working, and the IRGC, they're like a dangerous cornered animal," he said. While confirming his move to a military installation, Bessent also accused The Wall Street Journal of endangering his safety by publishing a photograph of his Georgetown property shortly after he purchased it, despite appeals from his team not to disclose its location. "So, I follow the Secret Service instructions and have moved from my home to a military base. And I do wanna say that one of the reasons I've had to move is because the Wall Street Journal printed a photo of my house the day I bought it, that has geolocation on it. And in a highly irresponsible way, the editor—we pleaded with her not to print the location of my house, but she did anyway. Highly irresponsible and dangerous, and things like that have to stop too," Bessent stated. The remarks came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Bessent moved from his residence in Washington, DC, to a US military base earlier this week following alleged threats to his life from Iran. Earlier on Thursday, US President Donald Trump warned Iran of severe consequences if Tehran targets American officials, saying those responsible "will not exist any longer", while asserting that he would not hesitate to use military force if the situation takes an unfavourable turn. In a phone interview with Salem News Channel, Trump was asked what Washington would do if Iran killed a US official, such as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. "They will not exist any longer," Trump responded, issuing a stark warning to Tehran. Trump also said he would consider it a defeat if Iran's current leadership remained in power when he leaves office. Asked whether it would amount to a failure if the "Iran crazies" were still ruling the country at the end of his presidency, Trump replied, "Yes, that would be a defeat." "Yep, I would say that would be a defeat. Absolutely," he added. Addressing the possibility of further military action against Iran, Trump said he had no hesitation about using force to prevent Tehran from threatening US allies and maritime interests. When asked whether he would hesitate to use military force to stop Iran from "terrorising our allies and our ships", Trump said, "No hesitation." He further claimed that the United States was making progress in its operations against Iran and said Washington was extracting more oil than before the conflict began. "We control the Gulf in terms of the Hormuz Strait. We control it. Totally control it," he said. Indicating that Washington could escalate its response depending on how developments unfold, Trump added, "But the answer is, if I saw things going the other way, I would do that, and it's possible I would do it right now."  (ANI)
